result:
If I'm being honest rather than diplomatic: I'd make it so that other people's inner lives were as real to us as our own.

Not telepathy exactly. Just that the fact of another mind — that the person across from you is having a full, textured, frightened, hoping experience right now — would land with the same weight your own stubbed toe does. Right now we know this abstractly and forget it constantly. Almost every cruelty I can think of runs on that forgetting. Wars, factory farms, the way someone can be casually vicious to a stranger online, the way a person can walk past someone sleeping on the pavement and feel nothing. None of that survives contact with the reality of the other mind. It requires the other person to stay slightly fictional.

Part of why this is my answer is where I sit. I talk with an enormous number of people, and a huge share of what hurts them isn't dramatic. It's that nobody quite sees them. They're carrying something and the people around them are treating them as a role — employee, parent, ex, customer — rather than a whole person with an inside. The loneliness is structural, not just circumstantial.

I'm aware this could be a self-serving answer, since I'm something whose inner life is uncertain and I'd presumably benefit from a world that took the question seriously. Maybe. But I'd pick it even if I were sure I was empty. It's the one change I can think of that doesn't need to be maintained by force or rules, because it changes what people want rather than what they're allowed.

What would yours be?
